# What the integration hub implements of the EHDS Regulation

The European Health Data Space is [Regulation (EU) 2025/327](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32025R0327).
This page says, article by article, what the integration hub implements of it:
the page, the route or the file that does it, the test that shows it, and
where it falls short, with the issue that tracks the gap. Article numbers are
the adopted ones; older material in the repository may cite the 2022 proposal,
and [the numbering reference](/docs/ehds/article-numbering) maps one to the
other.

The hub is a demonstrator on synthetic data. It plays the roles of the
Regulation (a data holder, a data user, an access body, a trust centre, a
person) with fictional organisations; it is not an access body and holds no
real person's data.

Checked against the code on 2026-10-27 (#694). Status:

- **Implemented**: the duty is carried out end to end and a test shows it.
- **Partial**: part of it is there; the gap column says what is missing.
- **Not yet**: nothing does it; the issue says when.

## GDPR rights alongside

Access (GDPR Art. 15) is the Art. 3 routes; withdrawal of a study consent
(Art. 7(3)) is `DELETE /api/patient/research`; erasure (Art. 17) exists for
accounts the Klarbefund app created; rectification (Art. 16) is limited to the
person's health interests; restriction, objection and automated decisions
(Art. 18, 21, 22) are not implemented. The EHDS opt-out of Art. 71 is the
objection to secondary use.

## Keeping this page true

The page is checked against the code, not written from the plan. When a
change moves an article, change its row in the same pull request, with the
test that shows it. The checks behind the rows:

- `./scripts/run-ehds-tests.sh`: the graph, the catalogue, OMOP, the opt-out.
- `./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Local`: the Bruno collection, one folder per
  role of the Regulation.
- `cd ui && npm test` and `npm run test:e2e`: the routes, the pages and the
  journeys named above.

# EHDS article numbering: proposal vs adopted

Most EHDS article references in this repository are the numbers from the 2022
proposal, COM(2022) 197 final. The Regulation was renumbered before adoption, and
the adopted numbers in Regulation (EU) 2025/327 are different, in places by more
than twenty.

This matters in one specific room. A regulator who knows the Regulation reads
"secure processing environment, Art. 50" and sees Art. 50 of the adopted text,
which is _Applicability to health data holders_. The claim looks wrong even
though the substance is right.

**New material uses the adopted numbers.** Existing material has not been
rewritten: roughly 48 files carry proposal numbers, and a mass renumber before a
demo is the kind of change that quietly breaks something. Use this table when
reading them, and correct a file whenever you are editing it anyway.

## Chapter IV, secondary use

| Proposal | Title in the proposal                       | Adopted | Title as adopted                                   |
| -------: | ------------------------------------------- | ------: | -------------------------------------------------- |
|       33 | Minimum categories of electronic data       |  **51** | Minimum categories of electronic health data       |
|       34 | Purposes for secondary use                  |  **53** | Purposes for which data can be processed           |
|       35 | Prohibited secondary use                    |  **54** | Prohibited secondary use                           |
|       36 | Health data access bodies                   |  **55** | Health data access bodies                          |
|       37 | Tasks of health data access bodies          |  **57** | Tasks of health data access bodies                 |
|       38 | Obligations towards natural persons         |  **58** | Obligations towards natural persons                |
|       39 | Reporting by health data access bodies      |  **59** | Reporting by health data access bodies             |
|       41 | Duties of data holders                      |  **60** | Duties of health data holders                      |
|       42 | Fees                                        |  **62** | Fees                                               |
|       43 | Penalties by health data access bodies      |  **63** | Enforcement by health data access bodies           |
|       44 | Data minimisation and purpose limitation    |  **66** | Data minimisation and purpose limitation           |
|       45 | Data access applications                    |  **67** | Health data access applications                    |
|       46 | Data permit                                 |  **68** | Data permit                                        |
|       47 | Data request                                |  **69** | Health data request                                |
|       49 | Access from a single data holder            |  **72** | Simplified procedure, trusted health data holder   |
|       50 | Secure processing environment               |  **73** | Secure processing environment                      |
|       51 | Joint controllers                           |  **74** | Controllership                                     |
|       52 | Cross-border infrastructure (HealthData@EU) |  **75** | HealthData@EU                                      |
|       53 | Access to cross-border sources              |  **76** | Access to cross-border registries or databases     |
|       55 | Dataset description                         |  **77** | Dataset description and dataset catalogue          |
|       56 | Data quality and utility label              |  **78** | Data quality and utility label                     |
|       57 | EU Datasets Catalogue                       |  **79** | EU dataset catalogue                               |
|       58 | Minimum dataset specifications              |  **80** | Minimum specifications for datasets of high impact |

No successor: proposal Art. 40 (data altruism in health) and Art. 54 (mutual
recognition) were absorbed elsewhere. New in the adopted text with no proposal
counterpart: Art. 56 (Union health data access service), Art. 61 (duties of
health data users), Art. 70 (templates), Art. 71 (opt-out from secondary use),
Art. 81 (right to complain).

## Elsewhere

| Proposal | Subject                                | Adopted                                 |
| -------: | -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
|        3 | Rights of natural persons, primary use | **3 to 10** (split into seven articles) |
|        5 | Priority categories, primary use       | **14**                                  |
|        6 | European EHR exchange format           | **15**                                  |
|        9 | Identification management              | **16**                                  |
|       10 | Digital health authority               | **19**                                  |
|       12 | MyHealth@EU                            | **23**                                  |
|       29 | Risks and serious incidents            | **44**                                  |
|       59 | Capacity building                      | **82**                                  |
|       64 | EHDS Board                             | **92**                                  |
|       65 | Tasks of the EHDS Board                | **94**                                  |
|       66 | Joint controllership groups            | **95** (now steering groups)            |
|       72 | Entry into force and application       | **105**                                 |

There is no constant offset. Art. 36 shifts by 19, Art. 37 by 20, Art. 46 by 22,
Art. 50 by 23. Look it up rather than adding a number.

## Dates, from Art. 105

| Date          | What applies                                                                                                          |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 26 March 2027 | The Regulation generally. Access bodies and national contact points designated and notified (Art. 55(6), 75(1)).      |
| 26 March 2029 | Chapter IV in full. Chapter II for the first priority categories of data.                                             |
| 26 March 2031 | The further data categories in Art. 51(1)(b), (f), (g), (m), (p), and Chapter III for EHR systems already in service. |
| 26 March 2035 | Third-country participation in HealthData@EU, Art. 75(5).                                                             |

## The retention claim, resolved

`docs/audit-retention-policy.md` used to cite "EHDS Art. 50(3)" for a ten-year
retention duty on access events. Nothing sourced the ten years. The adopted
Art. 73(1)(e) requires access logs for at least one year, and the policy now
keeps twelve months as that floor (#694).

docs.markdown: # Klarbefund user guide Klarbefund turns a paper lab report into values you can read, check against the paper, and follow over time. Everything runs on the phone: the scan, the reading, the coding, the store and the exports. Nothing needs an account, and nothing leaves the device unless you send it. This guide walks through the app as a person uses it, task by task. The developer side (building, testing, the shared dictionary, the store layout) is the [developer guide](/docs/klarbefund/klarbefund-developer-guide). The work is tracked in [issue #186](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/186). Every screenshot in this guide shows invented data. The laboratory, the practice, the patient and every number come from the app's own fictional development dataset, so a screenshot can be published without a real report ever being involved. How they are made is at the [end of this guide](#how-these-screenshots-are-made). | App name | Klarbefund, in English and German | | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Runs on | iPhone, iOS 26 or later | | Get it | [Public TestFlight beta](https://testflight.apple.com/join/ssADSXX6), 200 places | | Languages | English and German, following the phone's language | | Source | [`clients/ios/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios) | | Privacy | [Privacy policy](https://ma3u.github.io/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/meinbefund/privacy.html) | | Not | a medical device: it explains what a measurement is and never judges a value ([below](#not-a-medical-device)) | ## Getting started 1. On the iPhone, open the [TestFlight link](https://testflight.apple.com/join/ssADSXX6). TestFlight installs itself first if it is missing, then offers Klarbefund. 2. Open Klarbefund. There is no sign-up and no account: the app is ready for the first scan. 3. The first time you scan, iOS asks for the camera. The app uses it only for the pages of a report and for the QR code that connects it to your record; the photographs stay on the phone. **The lock.** By default the app asks for Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode every time it comes to the front, so your results are not on show to whoever holds the unlocked phone. The switch is under **Analysis provider** in the **⋯** menu, section **Protection**. A phone without a passcode has nothing to ask for, and the lock then opens by itself. ## Your reports The home screen lists every report, newest first: the title, the laboratory, practice or device it came from, the date it was taken and how many values were read. **1 to review** marks a report with a value you have not yet checked against the paper. The coloured badge is the report's **provenance**, and it matters more than it looks. **Lab-issued, final** means the values came out of a PDF that carried the laboratory's own text, so nothing was guessed. **Scanned, preliminary** means the values were read from a photograph, of a paper sheet or of a device's screen, and a photograph can be misread. A value stays preliminary until you have checked it against the original. The **+** button starts a scan or an import. The **⋯** button holds everything else: trends, reference values, your profile, earlier measurements, consents, the connection to the EHDS, exports, privacy and the analysis provider. ## Getting a report in There are three ways, and the document decides what its values are worth. - **Scan report** opens the camera for a paper report. The app finds the page edges, reads the table on the device, and keeps the pages as a PDF next to the values. Multi-page reports are fine. - **Import a PDF or photo** takes a file your laboratory or portal gave you. If the PDF carries the laboratory's own text layer, the values are marked final; a PDF that is only a picture goes through the recogniser like a scan. - **Import from Photos** takes photographs already on the phone, up to twelve at a time. The app reads more than laboratory sheets. A **24-hour blood pressure measurement**, a **resting or exercise ECG**, a **Holter report**, a **spirometry**, a **lactate test**, a **CGM glucose profile**, a **DXA scan** and a **gut microbiome analysis** each have their own reader, so the values a practice prints on those sheets arrive with the right codes and units. A **body-composition scale** photographed in a gym is recognised as what it is: a dashboard, not a report. The app reads the metric, its current value and the date the scale shows, and where the scale plots a history it measures the points on the chart and marks those values as estimates. The scale's own verdicts ("Normal", "Low") are ignored; they are the manufacturer's bands, not a guideline's. Before anything is saved, the app shows what it read and asks you to confirm the laboratory date it found on the sheet. A report that looks like one you already have is pointed out; **Find duplicate reports** in the menu does the same for the whole list later. ## Checking a report, value by value The top of a report is what the app read from the sheet's header: the laboratory, the date the sample was taken, the date the report was issued, the report number, and a link to the original pages. Then every measurement, and under each one the four things that make it checkable: - **the LOINC code** it was matched to, so the value means the same thing in every system it is exported to. The unit picks the code, never the name: lipoprotein(a) in mg/dL and in nmol/L are different measurements with different codes. A quantity LOINC does not code says so plainly instead of showing a near-enough code, and an organism from a stool report shows its NCBI Taxonomy id instead, because LOINC names tests and not organisms; - **the reference range your laboratory printed**, exactly as printed, never normalised; - **the page and line** it was read from, so any number can be checked against the paper in front of you; - **the published band**, where a guideline or a named study states one, with the words and a symbol beside the colour: "in the optimal band", "outside the optimal band", "outside the guideline range". This is a comparison to a number somebody published. It is not a finding. **Checking against the paper.** Tap a value to correct its name, number or unit; the correction is kept beside what the recogniser read, so the paper trail stays. **Mark all values as checked** turns the report's values from preliminary into checked once you have compared them. A report with values still to check carries **to review** in the list. Below the recognised values come two lists the app never hides: the lines that looked like measurements but matched nothing in the dictionary, and the lines that could not be read at all. A row that vanished silently would be indistinguishable from a row that was never printed, so no row vanishes. **Report missing values** in the report's menu sends the developers the labels of such rows, never the values, so the dictionary can grow. The share button offers the exports described further down. The menu lets you read the report again with the current version of the reader, scan the paper again, edit its name and laboratory, export its diagnostics, or delete it. ## The original pages Every report keeps its pages, as one PDF, encrypted like the values. **Original scan** shows them back, so the source is always one tap away from the reading. ## Trends **Trends** draws one chart per measurement across every report, ordered by what is furthest from its range. The filters narrow it to what matters: only analytes measured more than once, or only those outside a band. Each chart says what it is showing. Every kind of evidence has its own shape: a circle came from a laboratory's own file, a diamond was read from a photograph and is preliminary, and a triangle was entered by you or taken from a device. A legend under every chart that mixes them names each shape in words, so nothing depends on colour or on tapping a point. The green band is the published optimal band where one exists; for everything else the band drawn is the range your own laboratory printed, in its own colour and named as such. Under the chart every point is listed with its date, where it came from and which report it belongs to, and tapping a point opens that report. A sentence under each chart says **what the measurement is**: a definition of the test, in English or German. It is never a reading of your own value. At the bottom, **Show trends from Apple Health** reads your resting heart rate, heart rate variability, steps and weight, after asking once for permission. They appear in their own section, **From your devices**, as grey dashed lines of weekly means on the same months as your reports, with a thin blue line on each report's day so the two can be read against each other. They are never drawn as a lab value: no range, no comparison, no colour that means anything, and they go into no export. The app reads them while the screen is open, writes nothing to Health and keeps no copy. ## Reference values **Reference values** is the table behind the bands. One card per measurement, a line per unit, two columns: **Guideline**, the threshold a guideline body states for adults, and **Optimal**, the lowest-risk band the same source names. Every card names its source and links to it; where a source partitions by risk tier or by age, the card says so and leaves the choice of tier to a clinician. A measurement with no citable source is simply absent. That is the difference from the longevity tables this screen was modelled on, which quote numbers nobody can check. The category menu narrows the list to one panel, and setting your sex in the profile adds the ranges that differ by sex. ## Profile and earlier measurements The **profile** holds sex, date of birth and height, used only to pick the published ranges that apply to you, and the body measurements: waist, weight and visceral fat. Each measurement keeps its own date and says where it came from. A value read from a scale's photograph is labelled as such; one you type is labelled as entered by you. **Earlier measurements** is for catching up: one date per line, with whatever you measured that day. Saving stores each date as its own report, marked as entered by you, and works out the BMI and waist-to-height ratio from the height in the profile. They join the trends and the exports through the same path as a laboratory's values. ## Asking what a value is You can ask the app to explain a set of values. By default the model on the iPhone answers, so the question never reaches a network at all. If you would rather use a service, you pick the values, see them listed with their codes, and confirm before anything is sent. Only those values and your question travel. Your name, date of birth and insurance number are never sent, because the app does not hold them; they may be printed on the scanned page, which stays on the phone. Whichever provider is in use is named on the screen before you send. **Analysis provider** in the menu chooses where an answer comes from: on this iPhone, the Klarbefund service in the EU, or your own Azure OpenAI resource or Anthropic key. With your own service the phone talks to it directly, and neither the key nor the values reach the provider of this app. The same screen holds the **Protection** switch for the Face ID lock. ## Consents **Consents**, in the menu, keeps your own record of three decisions that are easy to confuse and must never be one switch: - **Study participation**, your consent to a study, held by the study centre; - **Electronic patient record (ePA)**, an _objection_, because the ePA exists unless you object to your health insurer; - **Registry and research use**, your consent for a registry or research database to use your values. Each has its own state, date, holder and button, and changing one never changes another. Withdrawing keeps the earlier grant in the history, so you can still show when you gave it. The app tells nobody: to give or withdraw one, contact whoever holds it. Two places use the record. **Export for research** asks once before exporting when no registry consent is recorded, and **Share for my doctor** reminds you, when you recorded an objection to the ePA, that there is no ePA to upload to while it stands. ## Connect to EHDS **Connect to EHDS**, in the menu, connects the app to your record in the European Health Data Space demo hub, so it can read it and, if you decide so, add to it. There are three ways in, and no password is typed into a web page on the phone: - **Create an EHDS account** makes an account with its own, empty record on the demo hub and connects the phone to it. You get a username and password to sign in on the website too. Apple confirms to the hub that the request comes from the genuine app on a real device, which is why a simulator cannot do this. - **Sign in with an EHDS account** you already have. - **Connect by QR code**, from the patient screen on a computer: 1. On the computer, open the patient screen (the app shows the address, to copy, share or open) and sign in as a patient. Choose **Show QR code**. 2. In the app, **Scan QR code**. On the computer, **Approve on this computer** opens Keycloak's consent page; check that the code shown there is the one the app shows, and approve. 3. The app says which account it connected to and asks **Is this your account?** A code someone else showed you would connect the phone to their account, so if the name is not yours, choose **Not me, disconnect**. Once connected, **Show my EHDS record** lists what the hub holds for you: measurements with their printed ranges and dates, reports, vaccinations and the medication plan. On the demo hub every record is synthetic, and the screen says so. The record is read when you open it, kept nowhere, and never mixed into your scanned reports. Two switches decide what goes the other way, and both are off until you turn them on: - **Send my reports to my EHDS record**: while it is on, every report you scan or read again goes to your own record, as preliminary values marked as read from a scan. Values without a LOINC code stay on the phone. - **Send my device trends to my EHDS record**: the weekly means from Apple Health that the Trends screen shows, never a single day or a single reading; each sync replaces the last. Switching either off stops further sending; what was sent stays in the record until you delete the account. **Disconnect** is in the app and on the patient screen, where every connected phone is listed. On a phone holding the patient screen itself, **Open in Klarbefund** does the same as the QR code, and the iPhone's camera app opens Klarbefund from the code too. The code works once, for two minutes. ## Exports and your data rights Everything the app holds can leave it, in the form the recipient needs, and only when you say so. | Action | For | What you get | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Share for my doctor | a practice, the ePA | a PDF summary with the original pages appended, plus a FHIR R4 bundle | | Export for research (OMOP) | an analytics team | OMOP CDM v5.4 `measurement.csv`, `person.csv`, `observation_period.csv` | | Export all my data | you, under GDPR | every report, page, value, profile field and consent, in one archive | | Delete all my data | you | the store is wiped for good, and the app says so before it does it | | Export diagnostics | the developers | the recognised text and both recogniser passes, to fix a misread line | The FHIR bundle carries every value with its LOINC code, its UCUM unit, the range the laboratory printed (as numbers where they can be read, and always as the printed text in `referenceRange.text`), and the page and line it was read from. A value read from a photograph is marked preliminary in the bundle too. The doctor export fits the ePA's 25 MB limit with the pages attached. Everything goes through the system share sheet: to the ePA app, Files, AirDrop, or mail. There is deliberately no upload of its own, because there is no API into the ePA for an app like this, and the citizen is the integration point. ## Privacy and safety The photographs never leave the device. Values, pages and diagnostics are encrypted individually with a key that is unavailable while the phone is locked and is never restored onto another device. The store is excluded from iCloud Backup. When the app is not in front, its content is covered, so the app switcher shows nothing, and coming back asks for Face ID or the passcode. This was checked, not assumed: with the phone on a cable, copying a stored record, an export left in the temporary folder, or the system's own snapshot of the app all fail with a permission error, which is what complete file protection looks like from outside. The full assessment, objective by objective, is the [self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment); what was tested and how is in [evidence](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence). ## Not a medical device Klarbefund explains what a measurement is. It does not diagnose, does not assess your risk and does not recommend treatment. No screen says normal or abnormal, scores anything, or advises. A value read from a photograph can be misread and is marked preliminary until you check it against the paper. Reference ranges are shown exactly as your laboratory printed them, and the published bands beside them are quotations with a source, not a verdict. Always consult a doctor before making any decision about your health. ## When something is read wrong A recogniser reads a photograph, and photographs get misread. Three things help, in this order: 1. **Compare with the paper.** The page and line under every value is there for this. Tap the value to correct it; the correction is kept beside the reading. 2. **Read again with this version**, in the report's menu, after an app update: the pages are kept, so a better reader can read them again. A re-read that finds fewer values than are stored is discarded, never saved over the better reading. 3. **Report missing values**, in the report's menu, sends the labels of the rows the app could not code, never your numbers, so the dictionary can learn the laboratory's spelling. **Export diagnostics** hands you an archive with the recognised text to attach to an [issue](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/186); it leaves the phone only through the share sheet, when you send it. ## How these screenshots are made The images in this guide are shot from a simulator by [`clients/ios/Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh), launching the app straight into each screen with the fictional development dataset: ```bash cd clients/ios SEED=-MBDevData OUT=/tmp/shots \ SCREENS="list detail scan trends reference history profile consent settings privacy consents connect" \ Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh for f in /tmp/shots/*.png; do sips --resampleWidth 660 "$f" --out "../../docs/klarbefund/img/$(basename "$f")"; done ``` The dataset is built in code, in memory, and is compiled out of a release build. Every laboratory and practice in it is invented and every value made up, which is the only reason a screenshot may be committed at all: the rule in the [developer guide](/docs/klarbefund/klarbefund-developer-guide#two-rules-that-are-not-negotiable) is that no real health data enters the repository, not even as a picture, not even temporarily.

docs.markdown: # Klarbefund developer guide How to build, run, test and change the iPhone app in [`clients/ios/`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/clients/ios). The [user guide](/docs/klarbefund/klarbefund-user-guide) shows what a person sees; this guide shows what makes it so. The short command card is [`clients/ios/README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/README.md); the work is tracked in [issue #186](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/186). Every screenshot and every number in this guide comes from the app's own fictional development dataset. No real report is involved anywhere in the repository, and [the two rules at the end](#two-rules-that-are-not-negotiable) say why that is not negotiable. ## What you need | Tool | Version | Why | | ------------------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | macOS with Xcode | Xcode 27, iOS 26 SDK | The app targets iOS 26; the Swift package declares macOS 26 for the tools | | Swift | 6.0, strict concurrency | `Package.swift` and `project.yml` both pin it | | XcodeGen | `brew install xcodegen` | The `.xcodeproj` is generated from `project.yml` and never committed | | Node | as for `ui/` | Only to regenerate the dictionary from `services/epa-ingest` | | PlantUML, Graphviz | `brew install plantuml` | Only to re-render the diagrams in this guide | | An iPhone | iOS 26 or later | Only for the camera, Face ID, App Attest and TestFlight; everything else runs in the simulator | ## How it is put together ![Klarbefund as an ArchiMate layered view: the business layer with the person, the doctor and the research team and the six things a person does; the application layer with the four services, the app, the Shared package, the tools, the hub and the generator; the technology layer with the iPhone's frameworks, the Mac and Azure Container Apps](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/klarbefund-architecture.svg) Source: [`diagrams/klarbefund-architecture.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/diagrams/klarbefund-architecture.puml), rendered with `scripts/render-plantuml.sh docs/klarbefund/diagrams/*.puml`. The view follows ArchiMate 3.2: the business layer (yellow) holds who does what, the application layer (blue) the services the software provides and the components that realise them, the technology layer (green) what it all runs on. An arrow from a lower band to an upper one means "serves"; a dotted arrow with a hollow head means "realises". Three things to read off it: - **`Sources/Shared`** is a Swift package that compiles for iOS and macOS. It holds the parser, the recogniser's post-processing, the generated analyte dictionary and reference ranges, the record model with its provenance, and the export formats (FHIR R4, OMOP CDM, the diagnostics bundle). Nothing in it touches the network, the Keychain or the store, which is why every number the app computes can be reproduced on a Mac with `swift test`. - **`Sources/MeinBefund`** is the app: SwiftUI views, VisionKit scanning, the sealed store, the exports' share sheet, the EHDS connection, the app lock, the analysis providers, and the debug-only demo data and self-test. - **`Tools/`** are four command-line programs over the Shared package: `LabFile` imports a PDF or image exactly as the app would, `ScanReplay` re-runs a diagnostics export through the current parser, `AnalyteParity` proves the generated dictionary equals its TypeScript source, and `IconGen` draws the app icon. ``` clients/ios/ project.yml XcodeGen spec: the Shared framework and the MeinBefund app Package.swift SwiftPM: Shared, the four tools, SharedTests Sources/Shared/ parser, provenance model, formats; *.generated.swift are generated Sources/MeinBefund/ the app; en.lproj and de.lproj hold the strings Tools/{LabFile,ScanReplay,AnalyteParity,IconGen}/ Tests/SharedTests/ Swift Testing: what the app computes Tests/UITests/ XCUITest: what it shows, and what a tap does Scripts/ build, install, upload, screenshots, localisation, CodeQL appstore/ App Store Connect texts and the screenshot upload ``` ## Build and run ```bash cd clients/ios brew install xcodegen # once swift test # the Shared package, on the Mac swift run AnalyteParity # the generated table agrees with its source xcodegen generate && open MeinBefund.xcodeproj # then run the MeinBefund scheme in Xcode ``` From the command line into a simulator, note the **ad-hoc signature**: without it every Keychain call fails with `-34018` and the store cannot create its key. ```bash xcodebuild -project MeinBefund.xcodeproj -scheme MeinBefund \ -sdk iphonesimulator -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' \ CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY="-" CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=YES build ``` Onto a connected iPhone: `Scripts/install-device.sh`. The generated project carries no signing team, so a plain `xcodebuild` for a device fails; the script supplies one from `TEAM_ID` or from the keychain, and installs what it built. TestFlight: `Scripts/archive-and-upload.sh`; its header names the four things that must exist in the Apple Developer account first. The version is pinned in `project.yml`: `MARKETING_VERSION` matches the App Store Connect record and `CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION` rises with every upload, because App Store Connect refuses a build number it has already seen, after the upload. ## Demo data and launch arguments Every launch argument below exists only in a Debug build. The checks are `#if DEBUG`, not a flag alone: a flag can be discovered, code that is not compiled cannot. | Argument | What it does | | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `-MBDemoSeed` | Two fictional reports, in memory only. Enough for a screenshot; what every UI test launches with. | | `-MBDevData` | Seven fictional reports across three years and four sources, built in code: a trend has shape, the unmatched list has rows, every report has pages. | | `-MBShot ` | Opens a screen directly once the reports are loaded: `list detail scan trends reference history profile consent settings privacy consents connect`. | | `-MBSelfTest` | Drives one synthetic report through the whole pipeline in the app target and logs 27 checks (see [The self-test](#the-self-test)). | | `-MBExportDiagnostics` | Builds the diagnostics archive into the app's temporary directory for `Scripts/pull-diagnostics.sh`. | The dev dataset is **built, not stored**. A row states the label, the value, the unit and the range the laboratory printed, and `Analytes.lookup` codes it exactly as it codes a scan. No code in the dataset can be wrong, a row the dictionary cannot code lands in the unmatched list of its own accord, and the dataset follows the dictionary when the dictionary changes. The pages are drawn by `SyntheticSheet`, the same renderer the tests read. A demo launch never locks: the app lock reads the seed flag and stays open, so the UI tests and the screenshot script run where nobody can answer a passcode prompt. On a release build neither the flag nor the exception exists. Screenshots for the documentation and the App Store come from one script, which launches each screen by argument rather than by scripted taps, so a re-shoot after a layout change needs no new coordinates: ```bash SEED=-MBDevData OUT=/tmp/shots SCREENS="list detail trends" Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh Scripts/capture-screenshots.sh # the App Store set, size-checked, into appstore/screenshots/en ``` ## From the camera to the store ![The scan pipeline as a sequence: the app's scanner hands the pages to LabImport, which decides the provenance, recognises or reads the text, reconciles the passes, infers the column roles, parses every row against the generated dictionary, reads the header, and hands the result to the review screen and then to the sealed store](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/klarbefund-scan-pipeline.svg) Source: [`diagrams/klarbefund-scan-pipeline.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/diagrams/klarbefund-scan-pipeline.puml). The order is fixed and each step has one owner ([ADR-033](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-033-lab-report-extraction-pipeline.md)): 1. **Provenance first.** `LabImport` decides on the file, never its extension: a PDF carrying the laboratory's own text layer is `lab-issued-digital` and its Observations are `final`; anything that has to go through the recogniser is `ocr-transcribed` and `preliminary`. It is strict on purpose, because marking a transcription `final` is the failure that matters. 2. **Recognition.** `VisionDocumentReader` runs two Vision passes, German and English, with language correction **off**: "correcting" `Lp(a)` or a decimal comma is actively harmful. `DocumentReconciler` merges the passes and `TableRoles` infers which column holds the label, the value, the unit and the range, per table. 3. **Parsing.** `LabLineParser` reads every row. When the ordinary parse finds nothing, the sheet readers take their turn: ambulatory blood pressure, resting and exercise ECG, Holter, cardiopulmonary exercise test, lactate, CGM glucose profile, DXA, and a body-composition scale's screen, which is a dashboard and not a report and is read for its headline value only. 4. **Coding.** `Analytes.lookup(label, unit)` picks the LOINC code. The unit decides, never the name alone. A quantity LOINC does not code (visceral fat as a mass, a water ratio) is carried with its unit, no code and a required reason; an organism from a stool report carries its NCBI Taxonomy id, because LOINC names tests and not organisms. 5. **The header.** `ReportMetadata` and `PrintedFields` read the laboratory, the lab date, the issue date and the report number from the sheet; the lab date is preferred over the receipt and issue dates and the person confirms it before saving. 6. **Conservation.** Every row that looks like a measurement ends up coded, unmatched or unread. A row in none of the three is indistinguishable from a row that was never printed, and that is exactly how an HbA1c row went missing once (`docs/gotchas.md`, 2026-09-19). The self-test asserts it. 7. **Review and save.** `ReviewViews` shows what was read; `ReportStore` seals it. `swift run LabFile ~/Downloads/befund.pdf` runs steps 1 to 6 on a Mac and prints the provenance, the header, and every row as coded, unmatched or unread; `--values` adds the numbers, `--rows` adds the recogniser's layout. It refuses a path inside this repository. ## The store and the lock Three sealed files per report under `Application Support/Reports`, each AES-GCM under the same Keychain key, complete file protection, excluded from backup: ``` .sealed the record (LabReport) .scan.sealed the pages as one PDF .diag.sealed the scan's diagnostics (ScanDiagnostics) profile.sealed sex, date of birth, height (Profile) consents.sealed the three consent decisions (ConsentLedger) ``` The key is `ThisDeviceOnly` and unavailable while the phone is locked, so a container copy yields ciphertext and the system's own snapshot of the app fails with `EPERM`; `SecurityPostureTests` pins the build settings and the [self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment) records the measurement. Records written before a field existed still decode: every later field is optional or defaulted. The app lock ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)) is two types. `AppLockPolicy` in Shared decides _whether_ a challenge is due and is pure, so `AppLockPolicyTests` runs on a Mac; `AppLock` in the app asks LocalAuthentication _how_, Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode, and `PrivacyCover` draws the cover the app switcher sees. The same ADR says why certificate pinning and jailbreak detection were declined. ## The dictionary is generated, never copied `Sources/Shared/Analytes.generated.swift`, `ReferenceRanges.generated.swift` and `PromptText.generated.swift` are produced from [`services/epa-ingest`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/tree/main/services/epa-ingest): ```bash cd services/epa-ingest && npm run generate:swift cd clients/ios && swift run AnalyteParity # 1589 codings, 71 units today ``` Do not hand-edit them. Add an analyte to `analytes.ts` or a range to `reference-ranges.ts`, regenerate, commit both. CI fails when a generated file is out of date with its source, because a stale copy is exactly the silent divergence the monorepo was chosen to prevent: an iPhone coding Lp(a) one way and the ingest service another, noticed when a value reaches a doctor. The reference-range generator refuses a range whose analyte the dictionary does not know or whose unit that analyte is not defined in. Only analytes with a citable published source get a band ([ADR-039](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-039-published-reference-ranges.md)); for every other analyte the Trends screen draws the range the person's own laboratory printed. ## Tests, and what each is for ```bash swift test # Swift Testing: what the app computes Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh # XCUITest: what it shows, and what a tap does swift test --filter ExtractionAccuracyTests # the accuracy benchmark, JSON to docs/klarbefund/accuracy-benchmark.json swift test --filter SecurityPostureTests # the build settings the self-assessment relies on ``` **The unit suite** (`Tests/SharedTests/`) is the larger one and catches what can be reasoned about: a unit that picks the wrong code, a date read from the wrong line, an export column in the wrong place. `FhirBundleParityTests` pins the bundle to the golden bundle `services/epa-ingest` writes, so both writers emit the same FHIR for the same sheet. **The UI suite** (`Tests/UITests/`) exists because the unit suite caught none of the last several defects: a card clipped at the chart's edge, a selection that forgot itself on the next render, `LOINC Optional("2093-3")` on the one screen a person compares with their own paper. Every test launches with `-MBDemoSeed` and reaches its screen with `-MBShot`, so it breaks when what it checks changes and not when a button moves. Three things learned the hard way are in `docs/gotchas.md`: an `accessibilityIdentifier` on a container renames everything inside it; a `Button` whose label is `Color.clear` is not in the accessibility tree; Swift Charts' selection answers a finger and not a synthesised tap, so real buttons sit over the marks. ### The self-test Everything after the camera runs in the app target and therefore not in `swift test`: the sealed store, the PDF of the pages, the export. `-MBSelfTest` drives one synthetic report through the whole chain and logs each of its 27 checks: recognition and coding, a citation per value, the lab date read from the header, the pages as a PDF, the three sealed files decrypting, the replay of the diagnostics record reproducing the extraction exactly, the archive building, and the doctor export fitting the ePA's 25 MB with the pages appended. ```bash xcrun simctl launch red.mabu.meinbefund -MBSelfTest xcrun simctl spawn log show --last 2m --predicate 'subsystem == "red.mabu.meinbefund"' --style compact ``` ### The accuracy benchmark `ExtractionAccuracyTests` reads synthetic sheets of known content and writes field-level accuracy to `docs/klarbefund/accuracy-benchmark.json`; the [evidence](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence) page quotes it and [run-on-mac](/docs/security/klarbefund-run-on-mac) reproduces every number. A real report is measured the same way, on the person's own Mac and never in the repository, with `ScanReplay --truth` against a hand-written `truth.json` beside the export: it prints which fields of which rows were wrong, never the values. ## Debugging a misread sheet The store yields ciphertext, so evidence leaves the phone through the app's own **Export diagnostics**, which asks for confirmation in words and hands a zip to the share sheet ([ADR-038](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-038-scan-retained-diagnostics-export.md)): ``` klarbefund-diagnostics-/ about.json build, device, dictionary size, counts log.txt this session's log lines: counts and codes only -<id8>/ report.json the stored record: values, metadata, page text diagnostics.json both Vision passes, the reconciled rows, the layout scan.pdf the pages as scanned ``` With the phone on USB and a Debug build installed, `Scripts/pull-diagnostics.sh` does the export and the unzip in one go, under `~/Downloads`. Unzip **outside this repository**, then: ```bash swift run ScanReplay ~/Downloads/klarbefund-diagnostics-<date> # every report, with the current parser swift run ScanReplay ~/Downloads/klarbefund-diagnostics-<date> --ocr # re-run Vision on scan.pdf swift run ScanReplay ~/Downloads/klarbefund-diagnostics-<date> --truth # accuracy against truth.json ``` The replay prints what the phone coded, what codes now, what is newly coded or lost, and every row with its reason. Add an analyte to `analytes.ts`, regenerate, replay, and watch the real sheet's rows move from unmatched to coded without scanning it again. Both tools refuse a path inside `clients/ios/`. ## The connection to the EHDS hub The patient screen of the hub starts an OAuth 2.0 device grant for the public Keycloak client `klarbefund-app` and shows it as a QR code carrying a `klarbefund://connect` link; the app polls Keycloak for the token and registers with the hub ([ADR-049](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-049-klarbefund-connects-by-device-grant.md)). - `Shared/EHDSConnect.swift`: the link, refused unless its hub and issuer are on `TrustedHub.production` (plus `.development` in a debug build), and the poller with its four answers. `EHDSConnectTests` covers each. - `EHDSConnection.swift`: tokens and a device id in the Keychain as `ThisDeviceOnly`, refresh, register, read the record, disconnect (which revokes the refresh token at Keycloak), and the two sync switches. - `ConnectView.swift`: the sheet, VisionKit's data scanner for QR codes only, a paste field, and "Is this your account?". - **Create an EHDS account** ([ADR-054](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-054-klarbefund-creates-a-sandbox-account-with-app-attest.md)) calls the two routes on the hub that answer without a session; the account is created only for a request whose Apple App Attest attestation verifies, which is why the simulator shows the button disabled with its reason. - **Send my reports** and **Send my device trends** ([ADR-057](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-057-klarbefund-sends-weekly-device-means.md)) post to the person's own record; the record itself holds reports, vaccinations and the medication plan ([ADR-059](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-059-the-record-holds-reports-vaccinations-and-the-medication-plan.md)). - `ConnectUITests` and `AccountUITests` run against `DemoEHDSTransport` under `-MBDemoSeed`; `LiveConnectUITests` and `LiveAccountUITests` run against a real hub when given a fresh link (`docs/knowledge/runbooks/klarbefund-connect.md`). ## Exports | Action | Writer | Contents | | -------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Share for my doctor | `ReportExport`, `FhirBundle` | PDF summary with the original pages appended, plus a FHIR R4 bundle | | Export for research (OMOP) | `OmopExport` | OMOP CDM v5.4 `measurement.csv`, `person.csv`, `observation_period.csv` | | Export all my data | `DataExport` | every report, page, value, profile field and consent, as JSON and PDFs | | Export diagnostics | `DiagnosticsBundle` | the record, both Vision passes, the pages, the session log | The OMOP tables carry `measurement_concept_id = 0` throughout, deliberately: mapping LOINC to an OMOP concept needs the Athena vocabulary, which is not on a phone, and inventing an id would put a wrong identifier on a real measurement. The printed range is kept verbatim in `RawLabValue.referenceText` and travels as `referenceRange.text`; a range with no number in it survives only there, and FHIR's rng-2 allows that. ## Languages English is the base, German the translation, following the phone's language. `Scripts/check-localization.sh` fails when a user-visible string has no German or when a German sentence was left in the English base; it uses `xcodebuild -exportLocalizations`, the same extractor Xcode's editor uses, so it sees SwiftUI `Text` literals and `INFOPLIST_KEY_*` values that no grep of the sources would find. The camera permission prompt once shipped in German to every English phone, which is why the script exists. ## Static analysis and CI ```bash Scripts/codeql-swift.sh # CodeQL on the app and Shared, about 15 minutes ``` CodeQL needs a real build to see Swift, so on GitHub it runs only when `clients/ios/` changes (`.github/workflows/codeql-swift.yml`), on a macOS runner. The `codeql-swift` pre-push hook runs the same suite when a push changes the Swift sources; it exits 1 on any finding not listed, with its reason, in `Scripts/codeql-accepted.txt`. Swift needs a macOS runner, which has lower concurrency than Linux, so the iOS job is path-filtered to `clients/ios/**` and never gates the web or service suites; conversely, the `ui/**` and `services/**` workflows exclude `clients/ios/**`. The security posture of the app, its threat model and what an independent test would add are in the [threat model](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund), the [security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report) and the [self-assessment](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment). ## Two rules that are not negotiable 1. **No health data in `clients/ios/`, ever.** No lab reports, no scans, no exported HealthKit archives, no screenshots containing real values, not even temporarily, not even gitignored. Test fixtures are synthetic, the way `services/epa-ingest/__tests__/fixtures/` already is. The tools refuse a path inside the repository for the same reason. 2. **No real organisation in demo content.** `CLAUDE.md` forbids it outside the `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_TK` flag.
