# Production readiness assessment, October 2026

Well-Architected Framework (WAF) and Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF), applied
to the EHDS Integration Hub as it runs on Azure Container Apps on 2026-10-16.
Each pillar states what is in place, with the evidence, and what is still
open. The scores are the project's own judgement on a ten-point scale; none
of this is an independent audit.

| Pillar                      | Score    | In one line                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| WAF: Operational Excellence | 7/10     | Deploy on every merge, tracing and structured logs, sixteen runbooks; no alert rules, no on-call                     |
| WAF: Security               | 8/10     | Tested by the project with nine of ten findings closed; no independent test                                          |
| WAF: Reliability            | 6/10     | 400 users with no failed request, health checks everywhere, managed Postgres with restore; Neo4j one node, no backup |
| WAF: Performance Efficiency | 7/10     | Sized from measurements, 50 users inside every SLO; 200 users not yet                                                |
| WAF: Cost Optimization      | 7/10     | Everything stops off hours, cost per 1,000 requests measured; no cost allocation per tenant                          |
| WAF: Sustainability         | 6/10     | The stack runs a third of the week; no carbon-aware choice                                                           |
| CAF: Strategy & Plan        | 8/10     | The EHDS roles, the BSI standards and sixty-one decisions written down; no SLA                                       |
| CAF: Govern & Manage        | 6/10     | Retention policy, audit trail, incident clocks; no SOC, no named incident team                                       |
| **Overall**                 | **7/10** | **A measured demonstrator. Not an operable platform for real data; the gap is listed at the end.**                   |

The platform assessed: the hub and its connectors on Azure Container Apps in
`rg-mvhd-dev`, West Europe, 21 apps and 9 jobs. PostgreSQL on a Flexible
Server ([ADR-041](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-041-managed-postgres-on-azure-containerised-locally.md)),
Neo4j Community at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB ([ADR-056](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-056-neo4j-grows-to-2-vcpu-and-4-gib.md)),
the UI on whole cores with up to six replicas ([ADR-061](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md)),
Vault with its state on the Flexible Server ([ADR-046](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-046-vault-keeps-its-state-on-the-flexible-server.md)),
stopped outside office hours ([ADR-053](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-053-everything-stops-off-hours.md),
[ADR-058](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-058-azure-triggers-the-off-hours-schedule.md)). The
load numbers are the runs in [the results index](/docs/operations/load-tests); the security
state is the [security test report of 2026-10-15](/docs/security/security-test-report);
how the platform is meant to be run for real is the
[operational guideline](/docs/operations/operational-guideline).

## WAF pillar 1: Operational Excellence, 7/10

In place:

- A merge to main deploys to Azure (`deploy-azure.yml`); the deploy waits
  while a load test runs and pins the connector addresses on every run. The
  PR gate, the test, security, compliance and CodeQL workflows run on every
  pull request; `demo-smoke.yml` runs Bruno, Playwright and ZAP against the
  live hub.
- OpenTelemetry collector, Prometheus, Loki, Tempo and Grafana
  ([ADR-045](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-045-observability-and-regulatory-audit-trail.md));
  the proxy is traced (`src/tracing.ts`) and logs structured JSON with the
  caller and the run on every line (`pino`); every audit record carries its
  run. Logs in Azure Monitor for 30 days.
- Vault keeps its state across restarts, locally in a file and on Azure in a
  database on the Flexible Server with an unseal sidecar (ADR-046).
- Sixteen runbooks under `docs/knowledge/runbooks/`: deploy, seeding, realm
  drift, Postgres recovery, off hours, load and stress test, the audit chain,
  the Klarbefund connection.
- Every image carries a `HEALTHCHECK`; the crawlers expose `/metrics` and are
  checked on it; the seed phases are resumable.
- The documentation is published from the repository and checked in
  pre-commit, so the docs cannot drift from the files.

Open:

- No alert rules. The load dashboard, the audit chain and the Postgres burst
  credits are read by a person; nobody is paged.
- No on-call model and no named operator; the operational guideline
  describes the roles, the project cannot fill them.
- No feature flags beyond the demo switches.

## WAF pillar 2: Security, 8/10

In place:

- The [security test report of 2026-10-15](/docs/security/security-test-report):
  CodeQL, Semgrep, grype, npm audit, trivy, gitleaks, hadolint, shellcheck,
  the app's posture tests and 46 anonymous black-box checks of the live hub.
  Ten findings; nine closed, one reviewed and accepted (the published
  development key of the local compose stack; Azure takes its keys from
  Vault).
- The [threat model of the hub](/docs/security/threat-model-hub) and
  [of the app](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund), each mitigation
  naming the code or test that shows it; one CycloneDX bill of materials per
  deployable part ([SBOM](/docs/security/sbom)), checked against the lockfiles.
- Every API route needs a session ([ADR-044](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-044-every-api-route-needs-a-session.md));
  who sees a patient's identity is decided by role, never by a query
  parameter; the UI reads the graph directly and the proxy serves the data
  planes ([ADR-043](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-043-graph-access-direct-or-through-the-proxy.md)).
- Rate limits in the proxy, per user and per participant, measured under
  load; k-anonymity with a minimum cohort of five in the proxy's
  configuration.
- Operator secrets are Key Vault references ([ADR-036](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-036-operator-secrets-in-key-vault.md));
  the live `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` was rotated; participant keys live in Vault.
- Keycloak: login events kept seven days, the UI client's scope limited to
  the seven EHDS roles, the admin console off the internet, every privileged
  role behind the console guard. The app locks with Face ID or the passcode
  ([ADR-060](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-060-the-app-locks-with-face-id-and-answers-pinning-and-jailbreak-detection.md)).
- Only the hub and Keycloak have public ingress; everything else is internal
  to the environment.
- The [audit retention policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md): ten years for
  access, transfer, contract and permit records, two years for sign-ins and
  edge logs, applied by `/api/admin/audit/retention`, which cannot destroy
  the only copy.

Open:

- No independent penetration test of the hub and no TR-03161 test of the app;
  the report's last section says what each would add.
- No mTLS between apps and no private endpoints; the guideline asks for both
  before real data.
- Neo4j has one database user; access is controlled in the hub and the proxy.
- Secret rotation is written down, not scheduled.
- The operator accounts and `edcadmin` are on generated passwords in Key Vault
  only once `scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh` has run against the live realm.

## WAF pillar 3: Reliability, 6/10

In place:

- The stress run of 2026-10-06 reached 400 users with 0 failed requests out
  of 81,518, at 63.6 requests a second; nothing restarted. At 50 users every
  SLO holds.
- Every image has a health check and Container Apps probes come from it; the
  proxy drains on `SIGTERM`; every outbound call has a timeout; `/api/tasks`
  answers from its store when the connector fails and says so.
- PostgreSQL on the Flexible Server keeps seven days of point-in-time
  restore; the realm, the contracts and the task store live there. Vault's
  state is there too.
- The graph views are capped at the newest 30 access events, which removed
  the one request that could take the UI down.
- A deploy cannot land in the middle of a load run.

Open:

- Neo4j is one Community node on Azure Files with no backup. Its data is
  re-seedable synthetic data today; before any real data the guideline asks
  for Neo4j Enterprise or a managed graph with backups tested quarterly.
- No circuit breaker; a slow connector is bounded by timeouts only.
- From 200 users the latency SLOs break on the UI's CPU. The UI's new size
  (ADR-061) is applied by `scripts/azure/size-ui.sh` and not yet measured.
- The connectors' pages did no real work in the runs so far (the UI called
  the management API at the wrong address, pinned since); the next `load`
  run is the first with contracts and transfers under load.
- No chaos engineering; the stress runs are the nearest thing.

## WAF pillar 4: Performance Efficiency, 7/10

In place:

- Measured, not guessed: the ceiling moved from Neo4j's memory to the UI's
  CPU within one day of runs, and each size was decided from the measurement
  (ADR-056 for Neo4j, ADR-061 for the UI, with the
  [scalability per component](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-061-the-ui-scales-out-on-whole-cores.md#scalability-per-component)).
- At 50 users: API p95 155 ms, pages 43 ms, NLQ 217 ms, 21.5 requests a
  second. `/api/graph` inside the SLO after the cap and the resize.
- Neo4j at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB, heap 1.5 GiB, page cache 1 GiB; indexes for
  every FHIR query path in `neo4j/init-schema.cypher` (more than 70, three
  vector indexes).
- The audit chain's batch writer takes the write load; audited queries are
  not a ceiling (434 ms p95 at about 16 a second).
- Next.js compresses its responses; the static demo is served by GitHub
  Pages.

Open:

- No response cache on the catalog or the overview; no compression in the
  proxy.
- 200 users inside the SLOs is the target of the next `stress` run, after
  `size-ui.sh`; the per-stage p95 goes into ADR-061's table.
- No CDN in front of the live hub.

## WAF pillar 5: Cost Optimization, 7/10

In place:

- Everything stops at 18:13 UTC and starts at 05:17 UTC on weekdays,
  triggered by Azure as a managed identity; about 65 office hours a week. The
  decision followed a month that billed €741 against an estimate of €426 for
  a stack running around the clock (ADR-053).
- Container Apps scale rules: the UI on an HTTP concurrency rule of 15, one
  to six replicas; everything to zero off hours.
- The cost of a request is known: at list price the apps that serve a request
  bill about $0.60 an hour, about **$0.01 per 1,000 requests at 50 users**
  (ADR-061, from `20261006-2115-load-aca`); a 20-minute stress run at six UI
  replicas adds about $0.22.
- Cost guards watch the total (`cost-guards.yml`).

Open:

- One resource group, one bill: no cost allocation per tenant or per role.
- The cost per 1,000 requests from Cost Management over a `soak` window is
  still to be taken.

## WAF pillar 6: Sustainability, 6/10

In place:

- The stack runs a third of the week (ADR-053, ADR-058).
- Resource use is visible: the containers row of the load dashboard, Cost
  Management.
- The one wasteful request, the uncapped graph view, is gone.

Open:

- West Europe, no carbon signal in the schedule or the region choice.

## CAF

**Strategy and plan, 8/10.** The regulatory motivation is written per article
(Regulation (EU) 2025/327 in its adopted numbering); the
[operational guideline](/docs/operations/operational-guideline) names which
EHDS role operates which part and what BSI C5, IT-Grundschutz, TR-02102 and
TR-03161 ask of each; sixty-one ADRs record the decisions; the planning index
tracks the work. Open: a formal SLA for participants, which the guideline
puts into the operator's service contract.

**Ready, 7/10.** Azure from a merge; the local stack in one compose command;
the seed phases resumable; one Dockerfile per part with its bill of
materials. Open: the operator's own environment, which does not exist yet.

**Adopt, 7/10.** DSP 2025-1 TCK, DCP and EHDS compliance suites on every pull
request; the Bruno collection asserts every route by persona
([ADR-031](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-031-checks-must-assert.md), [ADR-032](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-032-persona-organised-api-collection.md));
2,317 UI unit tests, 1,145 Playwright journeys, 279 Swift tests. Open: chaos
engineering, and a rehearsal of the Neo4j 5 to 2025 migration
([ADR-030](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-030-neo4j-2025-lts-migration.md)).

**Govern and manage, 6/10.** The retention policy and the tamper-evident
audit trail exist (ADR-045); the incident clocks of GDPR and NIS2 and who
holds each are in the guideline (section 7); the EHDS roles have their
go-live checklist (section 10). Open: an SLA and its dashboard, an incident
response plan with a named team, change management beyond pull requests,
cost allocation per tenant, an independent test.

## What stands between the demonstrator and an operable platform

The gap is no longer in the code; it is in the operation, and the
[guideline's checklist](/docs/operations/operational-guideline#10-before-go-live-the-checklist-by-role)
lists it by EHDS role. The items the project itself can still do:

| #   | Item                                                                                                      | Pillar                   | Tracked in                  |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| 1   | `stress` after `size-ui.sh`, then `spike`, `soak` and `signin`; the per-stage p95 into ADR-061            | Performance, Reliability | #571                        |
| 2   | Alert rules on the load dashboard and the audit chain, and who is paged                                   | Operational Excellence   | open                        |
| 3   | A Neo4j backup, or Neo4j Enterprise or a managed graph, before any non-synthetic data                     | Reliability              | guideline, section 2        |
| 4   | Compression and a short cache on the catalog and overview responses                                       | Performance              | open                        |
| 5   | Secret rotation on a schedule: the Keycloak clients, the account service, the catalog token               | Security                 | guideline, section 2        |
| 6   | An independent penetration test of the hub and a TR-03161 test of the app                                 | Security                 | #655                        |
| 7   | Operator accounts and `edcadmin` on generated passwords in Key Vault (`scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh`) | Security                 | #671                        |
| 8   | An SLA with its dashboard, and the incident response plan with a named team                               | Govern and manage        | guideline, sections 7 and 8 |

# Security test report, 2026-10-15

A self-conducted security test of the Klarbefund app and the demo hub, by
the project, with the tools the repository can run: static analysis,
dependency and container scanning, secret scanning, configuration tests
and anonymous black-box checks of the live hub. **It is not an independent
penetration test.** What such a test would add is listed at the end. Every
number here is reproducible with the commands given; the raw reports of this
run are not committed (they carry paths), the scripts are.

| Item         | Value                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Commit       | `64737039` on `feat/186-insurer-report` (the fixes below were made on the same branch)                                                          |
| Date         | 2026-10-15, 18:34 to 18:58 UTC                                                                                                                  |
| Machine      | macOS 26.7.1, Xcode 26 (Swift 6.4), syft 1.51.1, grype 0.118.0, trivy 0.74.0, gitleaks 8.30.1, semgrep 1.176.0, CodeQL CLI                      |
| Scope        | `clients/ios` (the app), `ui`, `services/*`, the Dockerfiles, the Kubernetes manifests, the live hub `ehds.mabu.red` from outside               |
| Not in scope | The EDC connectors and Keycloak internals (the hub's own threat model, `threat-model.md`), Apple's platform, the model providers behind ADR-034 |

## Method

| Layer                  | Tool, what it checked                                                                                | Command                                                      |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Static analysis, Swift | CodeQL, security queries over 31 app and 51 Shared files                                             | `clients/ios/Scripts/codeql-swift.sh`                        |
| Static analysis, TS/JS | CodeQL in CI on every push (`codeql.yml`); Semgrep with the repository's own rules locally           | `scripts/security/scan-repo.sh`                              |
| Dependencies           | syft bills of materials, grype and npm audit against them                                            | `scripts/security/generate-sbom.sh`, `scan-repo.sh`          |
| Filesystem             | trivy: vulnerabilities, secrets, misconfiguration in Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests            | `scan-repo.sh`                                               |
| Secrets                | gitleaks over the tree and the last 200 commits                                                      | `scan-repo.sh`                                               |
| Build configuration    | `SecurityPostureTests` (9 tests): entitlements, privacy manifest, ATS, cryptography, PKCE, HealthKit | `cd clients/ios && swift test --filter SecurityPostureTests` |
| Behaviour              | The unit suites: 419 Swift tests, 2488 UI tests, 22 proxy tests on this branch                       | `swift test`, `npm test`                                     |
| Live hub, anonymous    | 40 black-box checks: route gates, redirects, dotfiles, CORS, headers, TLS versions, Keycloak console | `scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh`                     |

## Results

| Check                                               | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

## What an independent test would add

This report is the project testing itself with deterministic tools. It
does not replace, and the self-assessment does not claim, an independent
penetration test. Such a test, by a BSI-recognised laboratory or a
contracted tester, would add:

1. **A release build on a device**: runtime inspection of the Keychain
   items, the sealed store and the file protection classes with the phone
   locked and unlocked; the cable test repeated by someone else.
2. **Authenticated black-box testing of the hub** as each of the seven
   roles, in office hours: horizontal access between patients (`refuseForeignRecord`), the
   app token's scope, rate limits under load, the App Attest verification
   with a replayed or forged attestation.
3. **The TR-03161 part 1 requirement list**, item by item against the
   official document, which this project assesses only at the level of its
   objective groups (`docs/klarbefund/self-assessment.md`).
4. **Keycloak and EDC configuration review** beyond what the public
   endpoints show.

Until then, the status in the self-assessment reads "tested by the
project, independent test open", and this document is the evidence for
the first half of that sentence.

docs.markdown:
# Threat model: the EHDS Integration Hub

STRIDE, for the hub as it runs on Azure Container Apps: the UI and its API
(Next.js 15), Keycloak 26.8, the neo4j-proxy, the EDC-V connectors with their
IdentityHub and IssuerService, Neo4j 5.26 and the PostgreSQL Flexible Server.
Written 2026-10-16; each mitigation names the code, the test or the decision
that shows it. The app that connects to the hub has its own model,
[`threat-model-klarbefund.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund). What the project
tested and found is the
[security test report](/docs/security/security-test-report); how the platform
would be run for real data is the
[operational guideline](/docs/operations/operational-guideline).

The data on the hub is synthetic: 127 generated patients, fictional
organisations, forged load-test sessions. The threats below are assessed as
if the data were real, because the hub is a reference implementation for a
platform that will hold real data; where a mitigation is enough for the demo
and not for real data, the table says so.

## How to read this model

STRIDE asks six questions of every data flow: can the sender be spoofed, the
data tampered with, the action repudiated, information disclosed, the service
denied, privilege elevated. The system context in section 1 numbers the data
flows and the trust boundaries they cross; the sequence in section 3 shows one
complete exchange with the id of every threat at the step where it would
happen; the six tables then hold one row per threat with the flow it sits on,
its status, and the mitigation with the evidence. The evidence is a file, a
test, a script or a decision in this repository, so each row can be checked
without asking anyone.

Four attackers are assumed, and every row names at least one implicitly by
its flow:

| Attacker                        | Reaches                                         | Holds                                                        | Wants                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Anyone on the internet          | B1: the hub's pages and API, Keycloak's sign-in | Nothing; or a leaked cookie, token or password               | A patient's record, a session, the admin console, the platform offline                            |
| A signed-in participant         | B1 with a valid session, as its role            | A legitimate account in one role                             | Data outside its role or its permit, another patient's record, a louder voice than its rate limit |
| A peer connector                | B2 through the public control plane             | Its own DID and credentials; forged or stolen ones           | A contract it is not entitled to, data without an agreement, a false identity                     |
| An insider with operator rights | B2 and B3 through `az`, `gh` and the scripts    | Subscription rights, the deploy identity, the admin password | Secrets, a silent change, a cleared audit trail                                                   |

A fifth, the supply chain, has no flow of its own: a compromised dependency or
image arrives through the deploy (F7) and is treated under tampering (T-07).

## 1. System context: data flows and trust boundaries

![The hub's data flows and trust boundaries: the people, the app, a peer connector and the operator outside; the UI and Keycloak behind the internet edge; the proxy, the connectors, the crawler and observability inside the environment; Neo4j, PostgreSQL, Vault and Key Vault behind the data boundary; twenty-one numbered flows](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/hub-trust-boundaries.svg)

Source: [`diagrams/hub-trust-boundaries.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/security/diagrams/hub-trust-boundaries.puml),
rendered with `scripts/render-plantuml.sh`.

Three boundaries, and what crossing each one means:

| Boundary              | Who can send a request across it                   | What proves identity                                                                   |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| B1, the internet edge | Anyone                                             | The session cookie (NextAuth JWT), a bearer token from Keycloak, or a DCP credential   |
| B2, the environment   | The hub's own apps and jobs, over internal ingress | The caller header the hub sets (`X-Caller`), the catalog token, the connector's DID    |
| B3, data and secrets  | The environment only                               | The managed identity (Key Vault references), the Vault token, the database credentials |

The numbered flows (F1 to F21) are what the STRIDE tables refer to. The ones
that matter most, and why:

| Flow       | What crosses                                         | Why it is the one to watch                                                                                            |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F1         | Every page and API request, with the session cookie  | The only path an anonymous attacker has to the data; every route behind it needs a session (ADR-044)                  |
| F2, F8     | Sign-in and the token exchange with Keycloak         | A forged or over-scoped token is a forged identity for everything downstream                                          |
| F3, F4     | The app's bearer token and its account creation      | A phone is outside anyone's control; App Attest is what keeps account creation to the genuine app                     |
| F5         | DSP and DCP between connectors                       | The one flow where a stranger's software talks to ours by design; identity is the DID and the credential, not a login |
| F9         | The hub's call to the proxy, with the caller header  | The proxy trusts the header because only the hub can reach it; the boundary B2 is what makes that trust sound         |
| F10, F11   | The management API and the catalog token             | Full control of the connectors; internal ingress and one token in Key Vault are the whole defence                     |
| F14, F15   | Reads and writes to the graph, and the audit records | Where the patient data and the evidence live; parameterised queries and the hash chain are the controls               |
| F19 to F21 | Keys and secrets                                     | Vault, its sealed state and Key Vault; nothing here is ever copied into an app                                        |

## 2. Assets

| Asset                                                                          | Sensitivity | Where it lives                                  | Notes                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Patient records (FHIR, OMOP)                                                   | High        | Neo4j (B3)                                      | Synthetic today; the model treats them as real                                              |
| Who read whose record, the audit chain                                         | High        | Neo4j, hash-chained (B3)                        | Regulatory evidence (Art. 73); ten years ([retention policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md)) |
| Participant signing keys                                                       | High        | Vault, state on the Flexible Server (B3)        | Never leave Vault; ADR-046                                                                  |
| Operator secrets: `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, DB and admin passwords, the catalog token | High        | Azure Key Vault, referenced by the apps (B3)    | ADR-036; the live `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` was rotated after it had been a published default       |
| Sessions and tokens                                                            | High        | Cookie in the browser, bearer in the app        | NextAuth JWT; Keycloak access and refresh tokens                                            |
| Verifiable credentials and permits                                             | Medium      | IdentityHub (B2)                                | Membership, EHDS participant, purpose, quality label, the permit as a credential            |
| Contracts, transfers, tasks                                                    | Medium      | EDC state in PostgreSQL (B3), mirrored to Neo4j | ODRL policies, agreements, `TransferEvent` nodes                                            |
| Catalogue metadata                                                             | Low         | Neo4j, the connectors                           | HealthDCAT-AP; public by design                                                             |
| The graph schema and the code                                                  | Low         | GitHub, public                                  | The documentation is the schema                                                             |

## 3. STRIDE

![One data exchange as a sequence, with the STRIDE id of every threat at the step where it sits: sign-in and request through the hub, then the DSP negotiation and the DCP credential check in the connectors, then the transfer and the audit record](__BASE_PATH__/published-docs/hub-exchange-threats.svg)

Source: [`diagrams/hub-exchange-threats.puml`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/security/diagrams/hub-exchange-threats.puml).

Status: **closed** means a test or a build setting pins it; **in place** means
the code does it and a test exercises it indirectly; **demo** means enough for
synthetic data and named as open for real data; **open** means nothing does it
yet.

### Spoofing

| ID   | Threat                                 | Flow   | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ---- | -------------------------------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| S-01 | A connector impersonates a participant | F5     | In place | `did:web` resolution against the IdentityHub's DID document, one per participant; the DCP presentation carries the membership credential (ADR-007, ADR-009). Checked by `scripts/run-ehds-identity-checks.sh` on every pull request.                                                                          |
| S-02 | A forged session reaches an API route  | F1     | Closed   | NextAuth JWT signed with `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` from Key Vault; `requireAuth()` in every handler, pinned by `ui/__tests__/unit/api/every-route-needs-a-session.test.ts` (ADR-044).                                                                                                                                 |
| S-03 | A replayed credential presentation     | F5     | In place | The EDC-V DCP implementation binds the presentation to the request; the DCP checks of `compliance.yml` run it. Not re-verified by the hub itself.                                                                                                                                                             |
| S-04 | Keycloak realm or console takeover     | F2, F6 | Closed   | The admin console is off the internet (`guard-keycloak-console.sh`, F10 of the test report); the admin password lives in Key Vault; the realm is version-controlled and drift-checked ([runbook](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/knowledge/runbooks/keycloak-realm-drift.md)). MFA on the admin is for the operator (guideline, identity). |
| S-05 | A fake Klarbefund creates accounts     | F3     | In place | Account creation answers only a request whose Apple App Attest attestation verifies (ADR-054); the challenge is signed and lives five minutes.                                                                                                                                                                |

### Tampering

| ID   | Threat                                            | Flow     | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| T-01 | Cypher injection                                  | F14, F15 | Closed   | Parameterised Cypher everywhere; the NLQ engine refuses a query that would read a patient's identity unless the UI says the role may (`revealsPatientIdentity()`); tests in `services/neo4j-proxy/__tests__/`.                       |
| T-02 | Contract terms changed in transit                 | F5       | In place | TLS at the edge; the agreement is signed by the provider's connector. Mutually authenticated DSP endpoints are a guideline item for real data.                                                                                       |
| T-03 | A forged credential claim                         | F5       | In place | Credentials are issued and verified by the IssuerService and IdentityHub (EDC-V); the hub shows, it does not re-sign. An HSM for the issuer key is a guideline item.                                                                 |
| T-04 | Cross-site request forgery on a mutation          | F1       | In place | `SameSite=Lax` session cookie (NextAuth); the CSP forbids inline scripts; no mutation reads its parameters from a GET.                                                                                                               |
| T-05 | A state jump in the negotiation                   | F5       | In place | The state machines live in the EDC-V control plane (REQUESTED, AGREED, FINALIZED; transfers REQUESTED to COMPLETED) and are leased in PostgreSQL; the hub mirrors, it does not drive. The DSP 2025-1 TCK runs on every pull request. |
| T-06 | The audit trail edited                            | F15      | Closed   | Each record carries the hash of its predecessor, SHA-256 over canonical JSON; `verifyChain()` reports any change, removal or reordering (ADR-045, `audit-chain.ts`). Both chains were intact after every load run.                   |
| T-07 | A supply-chain change in a dependency or an image | F7       | Closed   | One CycloneDX bill per part, checked against the lockfiles; grype and trivy on every push; npm audit in pre-push with time-boxed exceptions; images pinned; CodeQL. [SBOM](/docs/security/sbom), `security-scan.yml`.                  |

### Repudiation

| ID   | Threat                                           | Flow     | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| R-01 | A party denies a transfer happened               | F15      | Closed   | `TransferEvent` with sender and receiver DID and timestamp, in the hash-chained `dsp` chain (ADR-045).                                                                                         |
| R-02 | A party denies agreeing to a contract            | F5       | In place | The agreement is signed by the connector and stored in the EDC state; mirrored to the graph with its id.                                                                                       |
| R-03 | A read of a patient's record is denied or hidden | F14, F15 | Closed   | Every access the proxy serves is an access event in the `query` chain; the patient sees who read their record on their own page; retention ten years ([policy](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/audit-retention-policy.md)). |
| R-04 | An operator action leaves no trace               | F6, F7   | In place | Keycloak login events kept seven days; deploys are GitHub Actions runs; every live step is a script under `scripts/azure/` and recorded in the gotchas or an ADR. A SIEM is a guideline item.  |

### Information disclosure

| ID   | Threat                                                | Flow       | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| I-01 | An anonymous caller reads data                        | F1         | Closed   | Every API route needs a session (ADR-044); the pages that read them are in `PROTECTED_PATHS` and redirect; 40 black-box checks of the live hub confirm the 401s and redirects (`check-hub-blackbox.sh`).                               |
| I-02 | The connectors' management API reachable from outside | F10        | In place | Internal ingress only; the UI reaches it by its internal name, pinned on every deploy (#648). The catalog crawler sends its token only to listed hosts.                                                                                |
| I-03 | Secrets in the page or the repository                 | F1, F7     | Closed   | Server-side environment only; Key Vault references (ADR-036); gitleaks in the hooks and in CI; a test asserts no secret reaches the HTML.                                                                                              |
| I-04 | Cross-site scripting exfiltrates a session            | F1         | Closed   | A per-request nonce in the CSP with `strict-dynamic`, no `unsafe-inline` for scripts; `HttpOnly` session cookie; headers pinned by `next.config.js` and checked black-box. The off-hours page missed some headers once (F8, observe).  |
| I-05 | A database reachable from the internet                | F14 to F20 | Closed   | Neo4j, PostgreSQL and Vault have no public ingress; the Flexible Server allows the environment only.                                                                                                                                   |
| I-06 | Clickjacking                                          | F1         | Closed   | `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`, black-box checked.                                                                                                                                                               |
| I-07 | Re-identification from a cohort                       | F9, F12    | In place | `MIN_COHORT_SIZE` of 5 in the proxy for federated queries; roles other than the holder and the operator see a pseudonym, the birth year and no residence (#475). Output control by the access body is a process the demo does not run. |
| I-08 | An expired or revoked credential accepted             | F5         | Demo     | The IdentityHub checks expiry; there is no revocation list in the demo. Status lists and a revocation procedure are guideline items for real data.                                                                                     |
| I-09 | Logs carry personal data                              | F13        | In place | The proxy logs counts and codes, the caller as a hash; Azure Monitor keeps 30 days; the operational logs are separate from the audit chain (ADR-045).                                                                                  |

### Denial of service

| ID   | Threat                                    | Flow     | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| D-01 | One user exhausts the proxy               | F9       | Closed   | Per user: `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` requests and `RATE_LIMIT_HEAVY_MAX` analytical queries per `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`; per participant ten times that for callers that name no user; the audit route has its own. Measured: 83.6 % refused before, 23.2 % after the per-user limit (2026-10-05). |
| D-02 | A flood of DSP messages at the connectors | F5       | Demo     | The EDC-V control plane leases its state machines in PostgreSQL and times out; no rate limit at the connector's edge. A WAF and rate limits per hostname are guideline items.                                                                                                           |
| D-03 | An unbounded query                        | F14, F15 | Closed   | `LIMIT` on every list route; the graph views capped at the newest 30 access events (#580), which removed the one request that took the UI down at 90 concurrent users; every outbound call has a timeout.                                                                               |
| D-04 | Load takes the platform down              | F1       | In place | 400 users with no failed request (2026-10-06); the UI scales on an HTTP concurrency rule to six whole-core replicas (ADR-061); health checks on every image; a deploy waits while a load test runs. The latency SLOs break from 200 users; measured next.                               |
| D-05 | The stack is off                          | F1       | Accepted | Everything stops off hours by decision (ADR-053) and the UI says so; a 24x7 contract removes the schedule (guideline, availability).                                                                                                                                                    |

### Elevation of privilege

| ID   | Threat                                             | Flow     | Status   | Mitigation and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| E-01 | A patient reaches an admin route                   | F1       | Closed   | `requireAuth(["EDC_ADMIN"])` on the admin routes, 403 for any other role; the role matrix in `.claude/rules/api-conventions.md`; Bruno folder `09 Access control` asserts it against a real server.                        |
| E-02 | A researcher reads a patient's identity            | F1, F9   | Closed   | `seesPatientIdentity()` decides by role; `refuseForeignRecord()` answers 403 for another patient's record; the NLQ proxy refuses identity reads without the UI's header (#475). Bruno `09 Access control/28` to `/30`.     |
| E-03 | Roles injected into the token                      | F2, F8   | Closed   | Roles come from the realm's claims only; the UI client has full scope off and exactly the seven EHDS roles in scope (#648, `wire-ui-client-scope.sh`); `auth.ts` maps nothing else.                                        |
| E-04 | The catalog token used from elsewhere              | F10, F11 | In place | One token in Key Vault, reaching the UI and the crawler as a reference; the crawler sends it only to `DSP_CATALOG_TOKEN_HOSTS`; a wrong token is 401, never a fall back to the session (ADR-020, ADR-036).                 |
| E-05 | A transfer without an agreement                    | F5, F12  | In place | The data plane hands out an EDR for a finalised agreement only (EDC-V); the hub records the `contractId` with every transfer. The TCK covers the protocol.                                                                 |
| E-06 | The operator account `edcadmin` on a demo password | F2       | Open     | `EDC_ADMIN` reads a patient's record without a contract negotiation. `scripts/azure/secure-accounts.sh` moves it and every non-demo account to a generated password in Key Vault; to be run against the live realm (#671). |

### Summary

| Category               | Threats | Closed | In place |  Demo |  Open | Accepted |
| ---------------------- | ------: | -----: | -------: | ----: | ----: | -------: |
| Spoofing               |       5 |      2 |        3 |     0 |     0 |        0 |
| Tampering              |       7 |      3 |        4 |     0 |     0 |        0 |
| Repudiation            |       4 |      2 |        2 |     0 |     0 |        0 |
| Information disclosure |       9 |      5 |        3 |     1 |     0 |        0 |
| Denial of service      |       5 |      2 |        1 |     1 |     0 |        1 |
| Elevation of privilege |       6 |      3 |        2 |     0 |     1 |        0 |
| **All**                |  **36** | **17** |   **15** | **2** | **1** |    **1** |

Closed and in place differ in how they are proven: a closed row has a test or
a build setting that fails when the mitigation goes; an in-place row relies on
the code doing it and on the suites that exercise it. Turning in-place rows
into closed ones is the ordinary work of this model.

## 4. What the demo accepts, and what real data needs

| Residual risk                                | Why it is accepted for the demo                                       | What closes it                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No revocation of credentials (I-08)          | Every credential is issued to a fictional participant by the demo     | A status list in the IssuerService and a revocation procedure; guideline, identity |
| No rate limit at the connectors' edge (D-02) | The connectors talk to fictional peers only                           | A WAF and per-hostname limits; guideline, edge                                     |
| No mTLS between apps (T-02)                  | One environment, internal ingress                                     | Private endpoints and mutually authenticated DSP endpoints; guideline, connectors  |
| Neo4j has one database user                  | Access is decided in the hub and the proxy, and the data is synthetic | Neo4j Enterprise or a managed graph with roles and backups; guideline, data        |
| Operator accounts on demo passwords (E-06)   | Nobody's real data is behind them                                     | `secure-accounts.sh --all-non-demo`; #671                                          |
| No independent test                          | The project's own tests are the evidence so far                       | A penetration test of the hub; test report, last section; #655                     |
| The stack is off outside office hours (D-05) | A cost decision for a demo                                            | A 24x7 service contract; guideline, availability                                   |

## 5. How this model is kept true

- A new API route needs a session or a superseding ADR; the test
  `every-route-needs-a-session.test.ts` fails otherwise.
- A new route that returns patient fields asks `seesPatientIdentity()`
  first, and the Bruno collection gets a request that asserts the refusal.
- Every change runs the security scan, CodeQL, the compliance suites and the
  black-box checks; a finding goes into the security test report with a
  status, never only into a commit message.
- The diagrams are PlantUML sources under `diagrams/`, rendered by
  `scripts/render-plantuml.sh`; a flow added to the system gets a number here
  and a row in the table that analyses it.

## 6. How to verify this model yourself

Every closed row has a check that can be run on a laptop or read in CI:

```bash
cd ui && npx vitest run __tests__/unit/api/every-route-needs-a-session.test.ts   # S-02, I-01, E-01
cd ui && npx vitest run __tests__/unit/api/patient-route.test.ts                   # E-02, I-07
scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh                                             # I-01, I-04, I-06, S-04 against the live hub
scripts/security/scan-repo.sh                                                      # T-07: grype, npm audit, trivy, gitleaks, semgrep, hadolint, shellcheck
scripts/security/generate-sbom.sh --check                                          # T-07: the bills match the lockfiles
./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Azure-Dev "09 Access control"                           # E-01, E-02, E-04 by persona, against a real server
scripts/azure/guard-keycloak-console.sh --check                                    # S-04: console 403, admin REST 401, master realm 401
cd services/neo4j-proxy && npm test                                                # T-01, T-06, D-01, D-03
```

The compliance suites (`compliance.yml`: the DSP 2025-1 TCK, the DCP checks,
the EHDS suites) cover the connector rows, S-01, S-03, T-05, E-05, on every
pull request. A row whose check is missing from this list is an in-place row,
and the next step for it is the test that would move it.

# Threat model: Klarbefund, the iPhone app

The hub's threat model is [`threat-model.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-hub). This one is
for the app in `clients/ios`, which runs on a person's phone, holds their
laboratory values and sends nothing anywhere unless they say so. Written
2026-10-15 against commit `64737039`; each mitigation names the code or test
that shows it, and `clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/SecurityPostureTests.swift`
pins the ones that are build settings. STRIDE, as in the hub's model.

## System context

```
   paper report ──camera──▶ ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   lab PDF ──files/share──▶ │ Klarbefund (iOS 26, Swift 6)  │
   Apple Health ──read───▶ │  OCR · coding · AES-GCM store │
                           └──────┬──────────┬────────────┘
                 optional, consent│          │optional, consent
                                  ▼          ▼
                 ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────┐
                 │ EHDS hub         │   │ explanation service      │
                 │ (ADR-049/054/057)│   │ on device by default;    │
                 │ OIDC+PKCE, App   │   │ hosted: Azure OpenAI EU  │
                 │ Attest, Bearer   │   │ data zone, or own key    │
                 └──────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────┘
```

Trust boundaries: the device (Secure Enclave, data protection, app sandbox)
is trusted as Apple provides it. Everything that leaves the device crosses a
boundary and does so only after a consent the person gave for that purpose.

## Assets

| Asset                                   | Where                                        | Why it matters                                         |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Laboratory values, reports, page images | the store, `ReportStore.swift`               | Art. 9 GDPR health data                                |
| The store key                           | Keychain, `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`       | decrypts everything above                              |
| Hub tokens (device grant, app token)    | Keychain, `ThisDeviceOnly`, `EHDSConnection` | write access to the person's own hub record            |
| App Attest key                          | Secure Enclave, `DeviceCheck`                | proves a genuine app to the hub when creating accounts |
| Consents and their history              | `Consents.swift`                             | the legal basis for every transfer                     |
| Diagnostics export                      | written on request only, ADR-038             | contains values; must never enter the repository       |

## STRIDE

### Spoofing

| Threat                                                    | Mitigation                                                                                                                           | Status |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| A fake app creates hub accounts or pushes data as the app | Account creation needs an Apple App Attest attestation the hub verifies (ADR-054); every later call carries the app token            | met    |
| A fake hub harvests tokens                                | OIDC discovery from the configured issuer only, PKCE S256, `ASWebAuthenticationSession`; ATS forbids plaintext (`OIDCSession.swift`) | met    |
| A fake explanation service reads values                   | The provider is named in the request the person approves (`CloudConsentSheet.swift`); HTTPS by ATS                                   | met    |
| Someone else at the unlocked phone                        | App lock: Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode before the cover lifts, on by default (`AppLock.swift`, ADR-060)                         | met    |

### Tampering

| Threat                                         | Mitigation                                                                                                            | Status   |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Stored records altered on disk or over a cable | Each record AES-GCM sealed (authenticated), key in the Keychain; a cable test could not copy stored data              | met      |
| A misread value treated as a laboratory result | Provenance keeps OCR values `preliminary`; only a laboratory's own PDF text layer yields `final` (`Provenance.swift`) | met      |
| A tampered build                               | App Attest proves the app to the hub, not to itself; jailbreak and debugger detection declined with reasons (ADR-060) | accepted |
| A dependency with a backdoor                   | No third-party package at all (`Package.swift`, `project.yml`, `docs/sbom/klarbefund-ios.cdx.json`)                   | met      |

### Repudiation

| Threat                                | Mitigation                                                                                           | Status |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| "I never consented to that transfer"  | Consent events with time, holder and effective date, revocable, with history (`Consents.swift`)      | met    |
| What was sent cannot be reconstructed | A sync is a FHIR Bundle with a SHA-256 fingerprint the app records (`EHDSConnection.swift`, ADR-057) | met    |

### Information disclosure

| Threat                                     | Mitigation                                                                                                                      | Status   |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Values leave the device without the person | On-device OCR, coding, analysis and export; the only network calls are the two optional ones above, each behind its own consent | met      |
| Backups or iCloud carry the store          | Store excluded from backup; `NSFileProtectionComplete` default; exports and diagnostics written with complete protection        | met      |
| The app switcher shows values              | `PrivacyCover.swift` covers the window when the app is not active                                                               | met      |
| Logs carry values                          | Log lines carry counts and codes only (`Logging.swift`)                                                                         | met      |
| A cloud question identifies the person     | At most 40 values, no name, date of birth or insurance number; the service enforces the same (`CloudAnalysis.swift`, ADR-034)   | met      |
| Transfer to a third country                | Default on device; hosted default Azure OpenAI in the EU data zone; the Anthropic option is opt-in and says "United States"     | partly   |
| Screenshots or screen recording            | Not prevented (iOS allows no reliable block)                                                                                    | accepted |

### Denial of service

| Threat                           | Mitigation                                                                                                                             | Status   |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| The hub is down                  | The app works without the hub; the record is on the device                                                                             | met      |
| A hostile scan floods the parser | Vision and the parser run on bounded images; a degraded scan loses rows, never hangs (`ScanningTests.swift`, `AccuracyBenchmarkTests`) | met      |
| Lost phone                       | Export in four formats for the person to keep; no recovery from the hub by design                                                      | accepted |

### Elevation of privilege

| Threat                                  | Mitigation                                                                                             | Status |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| Debug entry points in a release build   | `-MBSelfTest`, `-MBDemoSeed`, `-MBShot` are compiled out (`#if DEBUG`)                                 | met    |
| The app writes to Apple Health          | Read-only authorisation (`WearableSource.swift`); pinned by `SecurityPostureTests`                     | met    |
| The app token does more than the record | The hub scopes the token to the sandbox record of that account; `isSandboxUsername` on every app route | met    |

## Residual risks and what closes them

1. **App lock**: decided and implemented 2026-10-15 (ADR-060). (TR-03161 O.Auth)
2. **No tamper or jailbreak detection**: declined with reasons in ADR-060; the sealed store and App Attest are the controls. (O.Resi)
3. **No certificate pinning**: declined with reasons in ADR-060; ATS without an exception domain, managed rotation. (O.Ntwk)
4. **Hosted Anthropic option.** Opt-in, named on screen, but a transfer to the
   United States; the operator needs a transfer basis or must switch it off.
5. **Independent test.** This model and the tests are the project's own. An
   independent penetration test against a release build on a device, and the
   requirement-level TR-03161 gap list, remain open; see
   [`security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report).
